tournament_identification.finding: The OLBG tennis listings captured for 27 October 2026 span FOUR concurrent tournaments, not one: ATP Vienna (Erste Bank Open, ATP 500), ATP Basel (Swiss Indoors, ATP 500), WTA Tokyo and WTA Guangzhou. The Rolex Paris Masters does not begin until 31 October 2026, so none of these matches are Paris.

atp_rankings_official.note: L'Equipe's 26 October list and the ATP live rankings differ slightly because live rankings net off points being defended that week. Both are recorded; neither is smoothed.

Carlos Alcaraz: Current ranking No. 3 (as of 19 October 2026); career-high No. 1 (12 September 2022); career record 313-70 with 27 career titles.
2026 titles: Australian Open (defeated Novak Djokovic 2-6, 6-2, 6-3, 7-5), Qatar Open at Doha (defeated Arthur Fils 6-2, 6-1) and Japan Open at Tokyo (defeated Jiri Lehecka 7-6(7-4), ...).
Has beaten Karen Khachanov in all six of their previous meetings.
Returning to Vienna for the first time since 2021.
Already qualified for the ATP Finals.
Withdrew before the 2026 French Open with a wrist injury, his first absence from a major since the 2023 Australian Open; the wrist problem kept him out for several months.
Lost to Ben Shelton in a fifth-set tiebreak in the 2026 US Open quarterfinals.
Has never gone beyond the quarter-finals at the Paris Masters.
Novak Djokovic: Aged 39; 24-time Grand Slam champion; ranked 11th-12th with 3,090 points.
Won the China Open in Beijing in October 2026, defeating Alex de Minaur 7-6(7-3), 0-1 retired in the final. It was the 102nd ATP Tour title of his career.
On the way to that title he beat Alexander Zverev 4-6, 6-4, 6-4 in the quarterfinals and Daniil Medvedev 7-5, 5-3 in the semifinals, and beat Nuno Borges 6-3, 7-6(7-2) in the first round.
Runner-up at the 2026 Australian Open, losing to Carlos Alcaraz 6-2, 6-2, 3-6, 5-7 [recorded as 2-6, 6-2, 6-3, 7-5 from Alcaraz's side].
Lost in the third round of the 2026 French Open to Joao Fonseca.
Was eliminated in the first round of the 2026 US Open, only the third opening-round major loss of his career.
Returns to Basel for the first time since winning the title there in 2009; seeded 4.
Is chasing an ATP Finals berth and drops zero points this week, having played none of Vienna, Basel or Paris in 2025.
Set a record 84 Grand Slam appearances in 2026, surpassing Federer and Feliciano Lopez's joint mark of 81.
Ugo Humbert: French left-hander, ranked 38th with roughly 1,270-1,295 points.
Four of his seven career titles have come on indoor courts.
Beat Carlos Alcaraz in the 2024 Shanghai Masters final.
Was the 2024 Paris Masters runner-up and eliminated Alcaraz in the round of 16 at the 2025 Paris Masters.
Karen Khachanov: Ranked 24th with roughly 1,940-2,030 points; a seven-time tour titlist.
Has lost all six previous meetings with Carlos Alcaraz.
Won the Almaty Open in October 2025.
Stan Wawrinka: Entered the 2026 US Open as a wildcard.
